[Sept 2019] President Vital Kamerhe has announced a new initiative to gather the nation's child soldiers into a single unit: The Congo Corps of Future Engineers.

Congo, like much the rest of Africa, has a historically poor track record across the entire spectrum of human rights. In 2011 there were an estimated 30,000 child soldiers under 15 years of age in Congo, with ~500 more being conscripted annually.

The President has stated that in order to properly fulfill the role of an Engineer Corp, the child soldiers will need to be kept from combat and provided with a 5-year crash-course education in French and English literacy as well as health, basic history, and various engineering disciplines; many of which should be in high demand in the private sector. Kamerhe has also expressed interest in acquiring some rudimentary psychological counseling for those who have seen combat (i.e. most of them). He also hopes to instill a sense of national pride in an effort to reduce future corruption. Eventually, having a competent Corp of Engineers will help improve the nation's infrastructure.

The President further stated that all current conscripts are free to leave before their education begins, but those that stay are required to remain with the corp for at least 8 years, meaning that most of these young men will be won't be released from service until at least their low twenties. Future recruitment of minors under the age of 16 for combat roles are banned, although volunteers as young as 13 will be allowed to enlist and begin an education in non-combat support roles.

Congo has reached out to the other nations of the world asking for experienced teachers to help properly educate these children.
